form_source: Item numbers and labels as printed on a Vermont Department of Health retail food inspection report (form seen 2026-10-29 on vtdoh.safefoodinspection.com). Starred items on the form are critical.
note: Plain-English lines are the Btown Brief's own explanations of each form item, not the Health Department's wording. Critical items are the ones most directly tied to foodborne illness. Passing: score of 70 or higher and no uncorrected critical violations (Health Department FAQ). The 'code' on each violation (like 5-208.24) is a section of the Vermont Health Regulations for Food Service Establishments.
scoring: Each inspection starts at 100 and loses the item's debit points for each violation. Debit points per item are printed on the form; we do not hard-code them because the PDF layout makes them unreliable to read.

1.form_label: Supervision: person in charge present and knowledgeable
1.plain_english: Nobody on shift was clearly in charge of food safety, or the person in charge couldn't answer basic food-safety questions.

1(a).plain_english: Some food came from a source that isn't approved (for example, home-made or unlabeled supplier food) or arrived damaged or spoiled.

2.form_label: Food in proper containers, properly labeled
2.plain_english: Food was stored in the wrong kind of container or wasn't labeled with what it is (or, for packaged food, missing required label details).

3.plain_english: Food that spoils fast (meat, dairy, cooked rice, cut produce) was found too warm in the fridge, not hot enough on the line, or cooled too slowly. This is the classic food-poisoning risk.

4.plain_english: Raw food (like raw chicken) could drip on or touch ready-to-eat food, or the same surfaces or tools were used for both without cleaning.

5.form_label: Equipment able to keep food at temperature
5.plain_english: A cooler, hot-holding unit or other equipment wasn't able to keep food at a safe temperature, or there wasn't enough of it.

6.plain_english: Frozen food was thawed the wrong way, such as sitting out on the counter instead of in the fridge, under cold running water, or in the microwave right before cooking.

7.form_label: Unwrapped food: no return and re-service
7.plain_english: Food that had already been served to a customer, like an unwrapped bread basket, was being served again.

8.plain_english: Food wasn't covered or was stored where it could get dirty, such as on the floor, under a dripping pipe, or uncovered in the walk-in.

9.plain_english: Staff touched ready-to-eat food with bare hands, or food was handled more than it needed to be.

10.plain_english: Scoops, ladles or tongs in use were stored in a way that could contaminate food, such as with the handle down in the ice or flour.

11.plain_english: Staff with symptoms like vomiting, diarrhea, or an infected cut weren't kept away from food, or the business had no policy for it.

12.plain_english: Staff weren't washing hands when required, or were eating, drinking or smoking where food is prepared.

13.plain_english: Staff working with food weren't wearing clean outer clothing or a hat, hairnet or other hair restraint.

14.plain_english: Surfaces that touch food or ice (cutting boards, ice machines, slicers) were worn, cracked, hard to clean or made of the wrong material.

15.plain_english: Equipment surfaces that don't touch food (outsides of coolers, shelving) were damaged or hard to clean.

16.plain_english: The dishwasher or the three-bay sink setup wasn't adequate, working right, or set up correctly.

17.plain_english: The kitchen was missing food thermometers, fridge thermometers, or test strips to check that sanitizer is the right strength.

18.plain_english: Disposable cups, straws, lids or to-go containers were stored where they could get dirty, such as on the floor or unwrapped.

19.plain_english: Items meant to be used once (like disposable containers) were being washed and reused.

20.plain_english: Dishes and utensils weren't scraped or pre-rinsed before washing.

21.plain_english: Dishes weren't washed and rinsed properly, such as dirty wash water or the wrong water temperature.

22.plain_english: Dishes, utensils or food surfaces weren't being sanitized, or the sanitizer was too weak or the dishwasher's final rinse wasn't hot enough to kill germs.

23.plain_english: Wiping cloths weren't kept in sanitizer between uses, or the sanitizer bucket was too weak or dirty.

24.form_label: Cleaning of food-contact surfaces and utensils
24.plain_english: Equipment and utensils that touch food weren't clean, weren't cleaned often enough, or weren't air-dried before stacking.

25.plain_english: The outsides of equipment, shelves, or hood filters had built-up grease, dust or food debris.

26.form_label: Storage of clean equipment and utensils
26.plain_english: Clean dishes and utensils were stored where they could get dirty again, such as on the floor or uncovered near a hand sink.

27.plain_english: The water wasn't from an approved source, wasn't tested as required (common with private wells), or hot and cold water weren't available.

28.plain_english: Wastewater wasn't draining into an approved sewer or septic system, or sewage was backing up.

29.plain_english: There was a leak, a clogged or dirty drain, or plumbing that wasn't installed to code.

30.plain_english: Dirty water could flow back into the clean water supply, for example a hose sitting in a mop bucket or a missing air gap or backflow device.

31.plain_english: A handwashing sink was missing, blocked, used for other things, or missing soap or paper towels, or the bathrooms weren't adequate.

32.plain_english: A smaller restroom or handwashing issue, such as no handwashing sign, no covered trash can in a restroom, or a door that doesn't close.

33.plain_english: There weren't enough trash or recycling containers, or the dumpster area wasn't adequate.

34.plain_english: Trash containers or the dumpster area were dirty, overflowing, or uncovered.

35.form_label: Free of insects, rodents and pests
35.plain_english: Signs of mice, rats, cockroaches or flies were found, or doors and gaps weren't sealed to keep pests out.

36.plain_english: Floors were dirty, damaged, or made of a material that's hard to clean.

37.plain_english: Walls, ceilings or attached fixtures were dirty, damaged, or hard to clean (dust, cobwebs, missing ceiling tiles).

38.plain_english: Lights weren't bright enough to work and clean safely, or bulbs over food weren't shielded in case they break.

39.plain_english: The hood or exhaust fans weren't working well or were dirty, letting grease, steam or smoke build up.

40.plain_english: Staff had nowhere suitable to store coats and personal items, so belongings were kept in food areas.

41.plain_english: Cleaning chemicals, pesticides or other toxic items were stored near or above food, or weren't labeled.

42.form_label: Premises free of rubbish and clutter
42.plain_english: The building or grounds had trash, broken equipment or unnecessary items lying around, which can attract pests.

43.form_label: Separation from living or other areas
43.plain_english: Food prep wasn't kept separate from living quarters or other non-food uses of the building.

44.plain_english: Clean linens and aprons weren't stored properly, or dirty ones weren't kept apart from food.
